Implication: Preserves current income and avoids an immediate taxable sale. Tradeoff: Retains tenant, rollover, hazard and concentration risk; a wasting lease term can reduce marketability. Decision gate: Use when verified net bids do not compensate for conservatively valued remaining cash flows and reserves are adequate.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q, SEC

Metric: Competitive sale before the lease gets shorter
Implication: Can transfer tenant/rollover/hazard risk while remaining term is still financeable. Tradeoff: May sacrifice upside and trigger taxes, transfer charges and prepayment costs. Decision gate: Compare executable net proceeds with conservative hold value and the owner’s diversification/liquidity needs.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance

Implication: May collect more rent if the tenant performs. Tradeoff: Concentrates negotiation, vacancy and financing risk into a narrow window. Decision gate: Only justify with strong unit coverage, credible renewal intent, ample liquidity and a funded re-leasing plan.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC

Implication: Can lengthen marketable income without changing ownership. Tradeoff: Weak rent, concessions, options or guarantors can destroy value; long terms can trigger reassessment. Decision gate: Execute only if the risk-adjusted extension premium exceeds concessions and retained risk.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

Implication: A stronger lease may broaden the buyer/lender pool. Tradeoff: Extension negotiations consume time and may not improve net price enough to cover costs. Decision gate: Use a value-before/value-after analysis and confirm transfer/consent requirements.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

Metric: Wait for tenant renewal, then sell
Implication: Avoids landlord concessions if the tenant exercises a valuable option. Tradeoff: The tenant may decline, demand a reduction or control timing. Decision gate: Track notice deadlines and maintain a sale/hold fallback rather than assuming exercise.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC

Implication: Balances a longer income term with inflation protection and flexibility. Tradeoff: Reset disputes, caps and tenant affordability can limit protection. Decision gate: Model fair-market-rent procedures, notice timing and realistic coverage.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics · Los Angeles area CPI

Implication: May preserve a viable operator and avoid downtime. Tradeoff: A permanent rent cut can outweigh the value of added term. Decision gate: Require unit financials and compare the net present value against replacement tenant and sale paths.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q, SEC

Implication: Could improve rent, credit or use if the location supports another operator. Tradeoff: Downtime, improvements, commissions and entitlement risk can be substantial. Decision gate: Obtain credible replacement-user demand and a funded lease-up budget before relying on this path.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning

Implication: May unlock higher-value land use where legally and physically feasible. Tradeoff: Construction, entitlement, environmental, leasehold and market risk can overwhelm residual land value. Decision gate: Require title/zoning/environmental clearance, costed plans and preleasing/exit evidence.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning

Value: Tax tool, not a standalone answer
Implication: May defer eligible federal gain and preserve investable capital. Tradeoff: Strict timing, boot, state rules and replacement-asset concentration can reduce benefits. Decision gate: Use only after private tax analysis and replacement-asset underwriting; arrange intermediary before closing.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

Implication: Can reduce single-asset exposure and improve liquidity. Tradeoff: Tax drag and reinvestment risk are real; diversification is not a return guarantee. Decision gate: Compare after-tax risk-adjusted outcomes against continued concentration; obtain fiduciary advice.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

Implication: May fund reserves without an immediate sale. Tradeoff: Adds leverage, debt service, maturity and prepayment risk. Decision gate: Stress vacancy cash flow and lender covenants; do not use debt to disguise weak property economics.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
Source publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

Implication: May broaden buyers or spread eligible tax recognition. Tradeoff: Creates buyer credit exposure and delays full liquidity; tax treatment is fact-specific. Decision gate: Require collateral, underwriting and tax/legal review; not assumed available or beneficial.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

Implication: Can release some capital while retaining upside. Tradeoff: Governance, control, transfer restrictions and reassessment can be complex. Decision gate: Value the retained interest and minority discount; obtain legal/tax advice before marketing.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

Implication: May align with philanthropic or intergenerational goals. Tradeoff: Irreversibility, liquidity and complex valuation/tax rules make this unsuitable as a default. Decision gate: Only evaluate privately with qualified fiduciary and tax professionals; no personal facts are assumed.
Note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.
